chapter: The Blue Room and Lou Forbes band
title: Photo of the Blue Room band and its members
summary: Hirsch names the men in the Gordon Kirst band, where he played drums, and the cartoonist Joe Schultz.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So you played in this band. Yeah, this is me. All right. All right. Come around here. Did you stay in the blue room after this band? No. After that, we went to the fountain lounge. Oh, okay. See, one of this took about... That's the blue room. This is one of the actual dance teams. This is... Did you remember Joe Schultz?
Oh, the name only. You've mentioned him to me.
This is gone. He's dead. He's dead. What did Joe Schultz play? He played violin. But Joe Schultz drew this.
He was quite a cartoonist. He was quite very good. And he drew that of the program. And I've got every one of their signatures on it. Oh.
Whatever happened to Meyer Weinberg, by the way? He's dead.

Changed his name to Gene Meyer. There he is, right there. He used to have to stand on a soapbox. And this is Albert Kirst. He was behind the drums. Eddie... Eddie... He used to play bass saxophone. Eddie Powers. Eddie Powers.
So in this period, you were still playing drums, didn't it?
Yeah, I was playing drums. Oh, and Charlie Hartman. Charlie Hartman was playing trombone. Yeah. Frank Federico. Do you remember Polké Carrier?
Again, it's a name I've heard people say.
He was playing first trumpet. He was a very good... Well, he traveled, huh? He left here, didn't he? Yeah, he left. Was he with Tee Garden, maybe? He was with some name band. I don't know.
Yeah, I think that's the one. It's Red Bowman. Johnny Ronica.
Johnny Ronica. Where's Johnny? There he is. Yeah. And Frank Federico. Fitchin'. Don't want my mama. Polké Carrier.
Yeah, Johnny Sabo. He was quite a guy. Quite a good one. This was from Lou Forbes. I still see his cousins, I guess, or brothers.
